titleStmt.title: Percepts to recollections: insights from single neuron recordings in the human brain
titleStmt.author: Suthana
Fried

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Percepts to recollections: insights from single neuron recordings in the human brain

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: the response properties of single medial temporal lobe neurons in humans, from perception to recollection
span.quote: The medial temporal lobe (MTL) is central to episodic memory, yet the neuronal code underlying translation from sensory information to memory remains unclear.

span.label: what neuronal code carries the transformation from sensory information to consciously retrievable episodic memory
span.quote: The medial temporal lobe (MTL) is central to episodic memory, yet the neuronal code underlying translation from sensory information to memory remains unclear.

span.label: collects the properties of human MTL neurons - selective, invariant, late, tied to conscious perception, internally generatable, reactivated before recall - into one account of an explicit, abstracted code
span.quote: Recent evidence illustrates several striking response properties of MTL neurons. Responses are selective yet invariant, associated with conscious perception, can be internally generated and modulated, and spontaneously retrieved. Representation of information by these neurons is highly explicit, suggesting abstraction of information for future conscious recall.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Recent evidence illustrates several striking response properties of MTL neurons.

span.label: single-neuron coding in the human medial temporal lobe during perception and episodic memory
span.quote: The medial temporal lobe (MTL) is central to episodic memory, yet the neuronal code underlying translation from sensory information to memory remains unclear.

span.label: review
span.quote: In the current review, we summarize recent data afforded by key methodological advancements in human single neuron data acquisition and analysis ( Figure 1 , see Box 1 ).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: MTL neurons transform novel percepts into sparse, abstracted-yet-detailed representations, and it is this abstraction that later allows the representation to be summoned by either internal or external cues, producing conscious episodic recall
span.quote: Given the critical role of these regions in episodic memory, we posit that these responses are central in the transformation of novel stimuli to representations that can be later consciously retrieved as episodic memories.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Representations must carry both detail and abstraction (loss of detail) so that a partial internal or external cue is sufficient to reactivate them
span.quote: As such, these representations need to possess detail but also abstraction (i.e. the loss of detail), so that they can be later summoned by internal as well as external cues.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Entorhinal stimulation enhances memory by resetting the phase of the hippocampal theta rhythm, aligning encoding with a favourable oscillatory phase
span.quote: Interestingly stimulation of the entorhinal area reset the phase of the theta rhythm in the hippocampus, providing a possible mechanism for memory enhancement.

span.label: the hippocampus sits at the top of a multisensory hierarchy, receiving object information via perirhinal and spatial information via parahippocampal cortex
span.quote: Results were consistent with the anatomical hierarchy within the MTL; the highest percentage of neurons with modality-independent invariant responses was found in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex as compared to the amygdala or parahippocampal cortex

span.label: invariance crosses sensory modality: the same neuron responds to a concept presented as image, sound or written word
span.quote: Recently, it was shown that this invariance crosses modalities, meaning that MTL neurons may exhibit a selective and “invariant” response to a particular stimulus out of 100 images and do so independent of the sensory modality (visual image, audio, or written iconic representations) through which the stimulus was presented

span.label: selective responses appear only when the subject consciously recognises the stimulus, and are near-silent when recognition fails
span.quote: Using flash suppression and backward masking paradigms it has been shown that selective MTL responses are mainly triggered when accompanied by the participants’ conscious perception or recognition of the stimulus [ 37 – 38 ]. When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec. Conversely, if the subject reported no recognition of the image, the MTL neuron selective for that image is mostly silent

span.label: imagining a stimulus recruits the same neuron that fires when it is seen, and subjects can steer a display by modulating two such neurons
span.quote: Subjects were able to successfully control which image was projected by altering the firing rate of two independently selective neurons independent of the visual input of the stimulus on the screen ( Figure 3 ). These results highlight the power of internal representation to override sensory input.

span.label: hippocampal and entorhinal neurons reactivate just before a spontaneous verbal report of recall, and only those regions do
span.quote: While sustained selective responses during viewing of episodes was present in neurons of other brain regions such as amygdala and frontal cortex, the specific reactivation prior to reported recall was only present in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex

span.label: firing-rate correlation across successive time points within an episode grows with repetition and predicts later recall, proposed as temporal binding
span.quote: Furthermore, the degree of correlation of hippocampal neuronal firing rate across successive time points within an episode increased over subsequent repetitions of the same episode, and predicted subjects’ future recall performance [ 59 ]. These observations suggest a possible neural mechanism for binding of an episodic memory across time.

span.label: entorhinal white-matter stimulation enhances memory and resets hippocampal theta phase, offered as the mechanism
span.quote: Interestingly stimulation of the entorhinal area reset the phase of the theta rhythm in the hippocampus, providing a possible mechanism for memory enhancement.

span.label: The human single-neuron dataset is rare and constrained by what clinical circumstances permit.
span.quote: Although the data presented are rare and limited by clinical opportunities, it offers exciting future avenues for further exploration.

span.label: Recordings are only possible where electrodes are implanted for clinical reasons, restricting the tasks and settings that can be studied.
span.quote: Due to the obvious invasive nature of single neuron recordings, studies are done only in special circumstances where electrodes are placed in the brain for specific clinical reasons.

span.label: Sampling is biased to anterior and middle hippocampus, so anterior-posterior comparisons cannot yet be made.
span.quote: The majority of human single neuron studies to date report recordings from the anterior and middle portion of the hippocampus and systematic anterior-posterior analysis in the hippocampal axis will have to await future studies with larger neuronal samples.

span.label: No human perirhinal neurons have been recorded, so the proposed hippocampus/perirhinal recollection-familiarity dissociation cannot be tested.
span.quote: Since human single neuron studies to date have not recorded from perirhinal neurons, future studies are needed to investigate this dissociation between human hippocampal and perirhinal neurons and their involvement in recollection vs. familiarity.

span.label: correlation of single-neuron responses with conscious percepts does not establish that the region is necessary for them
span.quote: The correlation of single neuron responses in the MTL with specific conscious percepts does not imply that these regions are necessary for conscious percepts, yet these responses may reflect the link between conscious percepts and episodic memories that can be later consciously accessed

span.label: most stimuli used were highly familiar to the participant, so the responses may partly reflect familiarity
span.quote: The human single neuron studies we have discussed thus far [ 17 , 33 – 36 , 38 ] often used stimuli that were highly familiar to the participant (e.g. a family member or famous person/landmark) and thus may to some extent reflect familiarity.

span.label: the recognition-related responses were not stimulus-specific and so need not represent single memories
span.quote: It is important to note, however, that the responses in the previously discussed studies were not specific to individual stimuli and thus do no necessarily represent single memories. Rather, the hippocampal and amygdala neurons may reflect the judgment of recognition independent of recollection or familiarity of individual items.

span.label: no human single-neuron study has recorded from perirhinal cortex, leaving the key dissociation untested
span.quote: Since human single neuron studies to date have not recorded from perirhinal neurons, future studies are needed to investigate this dissociation between human hippocampal and perirhinal neurons and their involvement in recollection vs. familiarity.

span.label: recordings come only from patients confined to a hospital room who cannot navigate a real environment
span.quote: Due to the obvious invasive nature of single neuron recordings, studies are done only in special circumstances where electrodes are placed in the brain for specific clinical reasons. These often involve closely monitored patients limited to their hospital room who cannot navigate a real environment during recordings.

span.label: fewer than 100 neurons are recorded at once, scattered across regions chosen on clinical grounds
span.quote: In a given human microelectrode recording set up, such as in chronic epilepsy patient monitored with intracranial depth electrodes, the activity of less than 100 neurons are simultaneously recorded and these neurons may be distributed across several brain areas, which need to be clinically sampled.

span.label: spikes on one microelectrode probably come from several neighbouring neurons, especially in densely packed hippocampus
span.quote: However, spikes detected on a single microelectrode most likely originate from several neighboring neurons, especially within brain areas that have densely packed cellular structures, such as the hippocampus.

span.label: recordings are almost all anterior and middle hippocampus, so the anterior-posterior axis cannot yet be analysed
span.quote: The majority of human single neuron studies to date report recordings from the anterior and middle portion of the hippocampus and systematic anterior-posterior analysis in the hippocampal axis will have to await future studies with larger neuronal samples.

span.label: electrode bundles can be localised to about 1 mm but individual electrodes within a bundle cannot be separated
span.quote: When registered to the electrode image, bundles of microelectrodes can be localized to areas as small as 1mm [ 97 ], although separation of a single microelectrode from its bundled neighboring electrodes is still a challenge.

span.label: the place cell, transferred twice - literally to human virtual navigation, and metaphorically to concept coding in a cognitive multidimensional space
span.quote: The invariant responses to individual persons and landmarks observed in the human MTL may be compared to the striking place fields in rodents, which appear to encode particular locations in the animal

span.label: reactivation of a fear memory by stimulating specific hippocampal neurons, held up as the model for a causal human approach
span.quote: Since the pioneering observations of Wilder Penfield, focal electrical stimulation of MTL circuits has been shown to evoke old memories or the feeling of déjà

span.label: invariant here means invariant across physical form AND across sensory modality - image, sound, written name - not merely across viewpoint
span.quote: Thus a neuron may respond to a picture of the Sydney Opera House and exhibit no response to 50 other landmarks, yet also respond to many permutations and physically different representations of the Sydney Opera House, seen in color, in black and white, or from different angles. In fact, the neuron may also respond to the iconic representation, namely the words “Sydney Opera”, which is obviously quite different in its visual properties than the image of this landmark.

span.label: place cell is used twice over: literally for rodent and human spatial cells, and metaphorically for concept cells as place cells in a cognitive multidimensional space
span.quote: It has been suggested that the response pattern seen in humans are indeed “place cells” in a cognitive multidimensional space

span.label: recollection versus familiarity is a behavioural distinction operationalised by whether spatial position is also recalled; the hippocampal data are read as tracking memory strength instead
span.quote: These results are consistent with the view that the hippocampus does not differentiate between recollected versus familiar items in memory, rather it relates to the strength of the memory

span.label: declarative memory is defined here by what the SUBJECT can report, which is why the paper argues the question belongs to humans
span.quote: In particular the study of declarative memory, or memory for recent facts and events, is best studied in subjects who can declare their recollections.

span.label: ultra sparse coding, asserted for MTL - note that Rigotti2013 reports PFC representations are rather dense, a different region and the opposite value of the same construct
span.quote: To summarize then, the neural code which characterizes the representation of external stimuli in the MTL is expressed in the responses of individual neurons, which appear to be highly specific yet invariant, suggesting that neurons may respond in an explicit fashion to concepts such as a particular person or landmark. These responses appear to be preserved (i.e. invariant) through multiple representations of the same stimulus independent of physical features, independent of modality of sensory presentation, and in fact present even in the absence of the stimulus altogether such as in imagery responses. Obviously, a particular concept is not represented by a single cell alone, although the coding is ultra sparse

span.label: cites → Gelbard-Sagiv et al. on hippocampal reactivation before free recall - a paper independently tagged in this corpus
span.quote: Gelbard-Sagiv and colleagues [ 58 ] designed a study where participants were able to freely report spontaneous recollections of a previously experienced episode while MTL neuron activity was recorded [ 58 ]; participants viewed various video clips representing episodes (e.g. Simpson’s TV show clip) and later explicitly declared clips that “came to mind” (i.e. freely recalled). Interestingly, similar to the highly specific and invariant responses to individual persons and landmarks reported before, sustained responses specific to distinct episodes were observed. Strikingly, hippocampal and entorhinal neurons that were selectively active during the initial viewing of distinct episodes were similarly reactivated just prior to the verbal report of recall of those very same episodes.

span.label: supports → the view that MTL neurons code concepts explicitly and invariantly
span.quote: To summarize then, the neural code which characterizes the representation of external stimuli in the MTL is expressed in the responses of individual neurons, which appear to be highly specific yet invariant, suggesting that neurons may respond in an explicit fashion to concepts such as a particular person or landmark. These responses appear to be preserved (i.e. invariant) through multiple representations of the same stimulus independent of physical features, independent of modality of sensory presentation, and in fact present even in the absence of the stimulus altogether such as in imagery responses. Obviously, a particular concept is not represented by a single cell alone, although the coding is ultra sparse

span.label: qualifies → the inference from selective responses to necessity for conscious perception
span.quote: The correlation of single neuron responses in the MTL with specific conscious percepts does not imply that these regions are necessary for conscious percepts, yet these responses may reflect the link between conscious percepts and episodic memories that can be later consciously accessed

span.label: supports → the account of hippocampus as tracking memory strength rather than distinguishing recollection from familiarity
span.quote: These results are consistent with the view that the hippocampus does not differentiate between recollected versus familiar items in memory, rather it relates to the strength of the memory

span.label: extends → rodent place-cell physiology, by proposing concept cells as place cells in a cognitive space
span.quote: It has been suggested that the response pattern seen in humans are indeed “place cells” in a cognitive multidimensional space

span.label: conscious perception —causes→ invariant
span.note: selective MTL responses appear only with recognition and are near-silent without it; the paper frames this as perception gating the response
span.quote: Using flash suppression and backward masking paradigms it has been shown that selective MTL responses are mainly triggered when accompanied by the participants’ conscious perception or recognition of the stimulus [ 37 – 38 ]. When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec. Conversely, if the subject reported no recognition of the image, the MTL neuron selective for that image is mostly silent

span.label: place cells —distinct-from→ grid cells
span.note: listed together as rodent cell types, with grid cells among those NOT yet characterised in humans
span.quote: However, several other types of cells have been found in rodents and non-human primates such as “grid cells”, “border cells”, “head-direction cells”, and “time” cells [ 74 – 78 ], which have not yet been characterized in humans.

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · recollection —contrasted-with→ familiarity
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span named neither. This clause names both and sets them as the two mechanisms a recognition task can run on. — and the hippocampal data are read as NOT respecting the distinction
span.quote: These results are consistent with the view that the hippocampus does not differentiate between recollected versus familiar items in memory, rather it relates to the strength of the memory

span.label: MTL —part-of→ hippocampus
span.quote: Results were consistent with the anatomical hierarchy within the MTL; the highest percentage of neurons with modality-independent invariant responses was found in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex as compared to the amygdala or parahippocampal cortex

span.label: RETRACTED (RE-GROUNDED) · theta —causes→ episodic memory
span.note: RETRACTED: RE-GROUNDED. The old span described the coordination without naming episodic memory. This sentence names both and states the claim the edge records - 'implicate A DIRECT ROLE FOR theta-linked spiking activity IN episodic memory' - which is a stronger causal reading than the old span supported. — predictive rather than demonstrated causal; the weight carries that
span.quote: A tighter coordination between hippocampal single neuron spiking and the simultaneously recorded theta LFP oscillation during initial viewing of the image predicted the success of the formed memory for that image

span.label: recollection —contrasted-with→ familiarity
span.note: RE-GROUNDS Suthana2012-percepts-to-recollections-insights-from-sing[2]: the relation was always stated, the endpoint names were not in the span.
span.quote: recognition tasks can be completed using mechanisms of recollection or familiarity

span.label: theta —causes→ episodic memory
span.note: RE-GROUNDS Suthana2012-percepts-to-recollections-insights-from-sing[4]: the old span named ONE endpoint.
span.quote: These results implicate a direct role for theta-linked spiking activity in episodic memory.

span.label: The selective responses of human MTL neurons are invariant not only across different pictures of the same concept but across sensory modality, firing to the spoken name, written name or image of the same entity.
span.quote: Recently, it was shown that this invariance crosses modalities, meaning that MTL neurons may exhibit a selective and “invariant” response to a particular stimulus out of 100 images and do so independent of the sensory modality (visual image, audio, or written iconic representations) through which the stimulus was presented

span.label: Selective and invariant MTL responses are slow, typically occurring 300-500 ms after stimulus onset, far later than sensory-cortical latencies.
span.quote: The selective and invariant responses described above are of relative long latencies often in the 300 msec - 500 msec range.

span.label: MTL neurons increase firing to their preferred image only when the subject consciously recognises it, remaining largely silent when the same image is presented but not recognised.
span.quote: When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec.

span.label: Subjects can volitionally drive the firing of individual MTL neurons to determine which of two competing images is displayed, overriding the actual visual input on the screen.
span.quote: Subjects were able to successfully control which image was projected by altering the firing rate of two independently selective neurons independent of the visual input of the stimulus on the screen

span.label: Hippocampal and entorhinal neurons that fired during the initial viewing of a specific film episode become reactivated seconds before the subject spontaneously reports recalling that same episode.
span.quote: Strikingly, hippocampal and entorhinal neurons that were selectively active during the initial viewing of distinct episodes were similarly reactivated just prior to the verbal report of recall of those very same episodes.

span.label: Tighter phase coordination between hippocampal spiking and the theta LFP during encoding predicts whether that particular image will later be remembered.
span.quote: A tighter coordination between hippocampal single neuron spiking and the simultaneously recorded theta LFP oscillation during initial viewing of the image predicted the success of the formed memory for that image

span.label: Growing correlation of a hippocampal neuron's firing across successive time points within an episode, built up over repetitions, predicts later recall of that episode.
span.quote: Furthermore, the degree of correlation of hippocampal neuronal firing rate across successive time points within an episode increased over subsequent repetitions of the same episode, and predicted subjects’ future recall performance

span.label: Hippocampal neurons discriminate old from new stimuli after a single trial regardless of whether the item's spatial position is recollected, suggesting they track memory strength rather than distinguishing recollection from familiarity.
span.quote: Results showed that single hippocampal neurons recorded during recognition could distinguish between novel (new) versus recognized (old) stimuli independent of whether spatial position was recalled and even after a single trial

span.label: Deep-brain stimulation of the entorhinal white matter during learning enhances later recall, whereas stimulation of the hippocampus itself does not.
span.quote: Suthana and colleagues [ 63 ] have recently shown that stimulation of the entorhinal white matter area, but not the hippocampus itself, enhances memory.

span.label: MTL neurons respond to a concept across radically different images and even its written name
span.quote: Thus a neuron may respond to a picture of the Sydney Opera House and exhibit no response to 50 other landmarks, yet also respond to many permutations and physically different representations of the Sydney Opera House, seen in color, in black and white, or from different angles. In fact, the neuron may also respond to the iconic representation, namely the words “Sydney Opera”, which is obviously quite different in its visual properties than the image of this landmark.

span.label: the invariance holds across sensory modality - image, audio, written word
span.quote: Recently, it was shown that this invariance crosses modalities, meaning that MTL neurons may exhibit a selective and “invariant” response to a particular stimulus out of 100 images and do so independent of the sensory modality (visual image, audio, or written iconic representations) through which the stimulus was presented

span.label: selective responses are late, 300-500 ms, and longer than those seen in animal studies
span.quote: Responses are late. The selective and invariant responses described above are of relative long latencies often in the 300 msec - 500 msec range. Interestingly and consistent with the anatomical heirarchy, responses in the parahippocampal cortex are significantly shorter than those in the hippocampus, amygdala and entorhinal cortex [ 35 ], but still with longer latencies than those observed in animal studies.

span.label: a neuron fires for its concept only when the subject reports recognising it, even at 33 ms exposure
span.quote: Using flash suppression and backward masking paradigms it has been shown that selective MTL responses are mainly triggered when accompanied by the participants’ conscious perception or recognition of the stimulus [ 37 – 38 ]. When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec. Conversely, if the subject reported no recognition of the image, the MTL neuron selective for that image is mostly silent

span.label: imagining a stimulus recruits the same neuron as seeing it
span.quote: Generating an internal percept of a stimulus through imagery in the absence of an external visual stimulus, recruits the same MTL neuron activated during viewing of the stimulus itself

span.label: subjects steered a display by modulating two independently selective neurons, overriding the visual input
span.quote: Subjects were able to successfully control which image was projected by altering the firing rate of two independently selective neurons independent of the visual input of the stimulus on the screen ( Figure 3 ). These results highlight the power of internal representation to override sensory input.

span.label: hippocampal and entorhinal neurons reactivate before a spontaneous report of recall; amygdala and frontal cortex do not
span.quote: While sustained selective responses during viewing of episodes was present in neurons of other brain regions such as amygdala and frontal cortex, the specific reactivation prior to reported recall was only present in the hippocampus and entorhinal cortex

span.label: the reactivation was visible in a single free-recall trial in a single neuron
span.quote: The highly specific reactivation was observed with a single free recall report, highlighting the robustness of this phenomenon that could be observed in a single trial in a single neuron under complex recording conditions in a hospital ward.

span.label: new selective responses to experimenters formed over hours or days
span.quote: For instance, MTL neurons responding to particular individuals participating in administering the experimental paradigms were formed over a few hours or days

span.label: several rodent cell types - grid, border, head-direction, time - have not yet been characterised in humans
span.quote: However, several other types of cells have been found in rodents and non-human primates such as “grid cells”, “border cells”, “head-direction cells”, and “time” cells [ 74 – 78 ], which have not yet been characterized in humans.

span.label: Episodic memory
span.quote: Episodic memory memory for events within a spatial and temporal context

span.label: Medial temporal lobe (MTL)
span.quote: Medial temporal lobe (MTL) the MTL consists of the hippocampus, entorhinal cortex, perirhinal cortex, and parahippocampal cortex

span.label: Spikes
span.quote: Spikes extracellularly recorded action potentials from single (single-unit) or multiple (multi-unit) neurons

span.label: Local field potentials (LFPs)
span.quote: Local field potentials (LFPs) extracellular voltage changes reflective of dendritic currents and action potentials of populations of neurons

span.label: Recollection vs. familiarity
span.quote: Recollection vs. familiarity recollection refers to being able to link a given memory to a specific place in time whereas familiarity refers to having a given memory without being able to assign its origin

span.label: invariant response
span.quote: Responses are Invariant. An MTL neuron may respond to a particular stimulus, such as a particular face or landmark, but in addition it will also respond to other stimuli representing that particular face or landmark, even if these stimuli are distinctly different in stimulus features compared to the original stimulus

span.label: declarative memory
span.quote: In particular the study of declarative memory, or memory for recent facts and events, is best studied in subjects who can declare their recollections.

span.label: spike sorting
span.quote: Currently, efficient analysis techniques have automated the process of spike sorting to separate pyramidal vs. interneuron and single- vs. multi-unit types by comparing waveform characteristics (e.g. shape and amplitude) and inter-spike intervals distributions

span.label: image display duration
span.quote: When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec.

span.label: single-neuron firing rate during stimulus viewing
span.term: single-neuron firing rate during stimulus viewing
span.quote: Single spikes (blue dots) for each trial (line) and averaged firing rate (red bars) across trials significantly increased during the viewing of the image of actor ‘Josh Brolin’.

span.label: spike-field coherence between hippocampal spiking and theta LFP
span.term: spike-field coherence between hippocampal spiking and theta LFP
span.quote: Strength of the phase locking (i.e. spike-field coherence [SFC] percentage) of single neuron firing rate during learning is significantly higher for subsequently remembered versus forgotten images in the 2–10 Hz frequency band.

span.label: firing rate during stimulus viewing
span.quote: Responses are Selective. MTL neurons can respond to particular stimulus categories (e.g. faces, outdoor scenes, animals, etc.) or to individual stimuli (e.g. a family member, a famous individual, or a particular landmark) during the passive viewing of visual stimuli

span.label: subsequently remembered versus forgotten
span.quote: A tighter coordination between hippocampal single neuron spiking and the simultaneously recorded theta LFP oscillation during initial viewing of the image predicted the success of the formed memory for that image

span.label: response latency by MTL subregion
span.quote: Responses are late. The selective and invariant responses described above are of relative long latencies often in the 300 msec - 500 msec range. Interestingly and consistent with the anatomical heirarchy, responses in the parahippocampal cortex are significantly shorter than those in the hippocampus, amygdala and entorhinal cortex [ 35 ], but still with longer latencies than those observed in animal studies.

span.label: 300 msec - 500 msec — typical latency range of selective, invariant MTL single-neuron responses
span.quote: The selective and invariant responses described above are of relative long latencies often in the 300 msec - 500 msec range.

span.label: 33 to 256 msec — range of image display durations used to dissociate conscious recognition from stimulus presence
span.quote: When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec.

span.label: 3–8Hz — frequency band of the theta LFP oscillation implicated in human memory
span.quote: Theta LFP oscillations (3–8Hz) have been widely implicated in human memory

span.label: 30–100 Hz — frequency band of the gamma oscillation linked to the recall-predicting theta amplitude
span.quote: the theta amplitude that predicted recall success was also strongly linked to the gamma oscillation (30–100 Hz;

span.label: 100 images (50 old and 50 new stimuli) — size and composition of the recognition-memory test set in the spike-theta encoding study
span.quote: During the memory test, subjects were shown a new set of 100 images (50 old and 50 new stimuli) and were asked to report whether they had seen a presented image before.

span.label: 7 out of 8 — trials on which one example subject successfully faded the target actor's image by controlling neuronal firing
span.quote: The example subject shown succeeded 7 out of 8 trials when instructed to display or ‘fade’ the image of Brolin onto the computer screen.

span.label: less than 100 — number of neurons that can currently be recorded simultaneously in a human depth-electrode setup
span.quote: the activity of less than 100 neurons are simultaneously recorded

span.label: 300 to 500 ms — latency of selective invariant responses
span.quote: Responses are late. The selective and invariant responses described above are of relative long latencies often in the 300 msec - 500 msec range. Interestingly and consistent with the anatomical heirarchy, responses in the parahippocampal cortex are significantly shorter than those in the hippocampus, amygdala and entorhinal cortex [ 35 ], but still with longer latencies than those observed in animal studies.

span.label: 33 to 256 ms — the display-time range over which recognition gates the response
span.quote: Using flash suppression and backward masking paradigms it has been shown that selective MTL responses are mainly triggered when accompanied by the participants’ conscious perception or recognition of the stimulus [ 37 – 38 ]. When varying the display time of an image between 33 to 256 msec, MTL neurons selective for an image significantly increase in firing rate only if the image is recognized by the subject, even if the image is presented for as briefly as 33 msec. Conversely, if the subject reported no recognition of the image, the MTL neuron selective for that image is mostly silent

span.label: 3 to 8 Hz theta — the oscillation predicting encoding success
span.quote: Theta LFP oscillations (3–8Hz) have been widely implicated in human memory (for review see [ 43 – 44 ]) and the strength of their amplitude measured in the MTL has been shown to predict the success of episodic encoding in humans

span.label: fewer than 100 neurons simultaneously — the ceiling of the human recording setup
span.quote: In a given human microelectrode recording set up, such as in chronic epilepsy patient monitored with intracranial depth electrodes, the activity of less than 100 neurons are simultaneously recorded and these neurons may be distributed across several brain areas, which need to be clinically sampled.

span.label: about 1 mm — the precision to which an electrode bundle can be localised
span.quote: When registered to the electrode image, bundles of microelectrodes can be localized to areas as small as 1mm [ 97 ], although separation of a single microelectrode from its bundled neighboring electrodes is still a challenge.

span.label: spike-field coherence
span.quote: A tighter coordination between hippocampal single neuron spiking and the simultaneously recorded theta LFP oscillation during initial viewing of the image predicted the success of the formed memory for that image
